name: Zero-loss audit requirements require persistent sink configuration

input.source_text: class B {} module M { public fun run() -> Object { RevisionHistory.configure_sink(); B.open() { |t| 1 }; RevisionHistory.prune(1); [try { RevisionHistory.events(1, 1) } catch e { e }, RevisionHistory.recover(1, 1)] } } M.run()

applicability.reason: Supported. C055 makes zero-loss audit recovery use a SEPARATELY CONFIGURED persistent Host or runtime sink, and forbids an unbounded in-memory subscriber queue from being the semantic guarantee. No sink existed, so there was nothing to configure and nothing to recover from. The sink is now its own store, configured by an explicit Host act rather than by a subscriber, and PRUNING retained history is what tells the two apart: the in-memory read then fails with AuditHistoryUnavailableError while the sink still answers the commit. With no sink configured, recovery offers no guarantee at all, which is exactly C055's point. C053's retained-history path is untouched when nothing is pruned.
